FKJ clears RADAR admission because the performance is built around a distinctive multi-instrumental live language in which keys, guitar, saxophone, vocals and live looping are part of the musical identity, and the Tokyo date presents the new Tyber album in the only announced Japanese performance of the tour. events.subtitle: Tyber Tour
events.factual_description: LIVE NATION H.I.P. announced FKJ: Tyber Tour for December 10, 2026 at Tokyo International Forum Hall A, with doors at 6:00 PM and the performance at 7:00 PM. The official event page identifies this as FKJ's first Japan performance in two years and the sole announced Japanese date of the Tyber Tour, which is part of a broader Europe and North America world tour. The new album Tyber is scheduled for release on September 11, 2026. The official page lists SS seats at ¥15,800 and S seats at ¥11,800 and links to an authorized Lawson Ticket artist presale opening August 26 at noon JST.

en.why_it_matters: FKJ's live identity is unusually physical for music that can look electronic on paper: keys, guitar, saxophone, voice and looping are assembled in real time until groove and arrangement become part of the performance itself. The Tokyo date arrives with Tyber as a new body of material rather than a catalogue stop, and the fact that Japan gets a single announced night gives the show a clear local reason to matter without turning a world-tour date into artificial scarcity.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for this night if December overlaps with Tokyo, especially if multi-instrumental performance, groove and the jazz-soul-electronic borderlands are part of the trip. It can anchor an evening in the city, while a genuinely singular master appearance or one-off elsewhere in Kanto would still take precedence.

es.why_it_matters: La identidad en vivo de FKJ es mucho más física de lo que su música electrónica puede sugerir en papel: teclados, guitarra, saxofón, voz y loops se van armando en tiempo real hasta que el groove y el arreglo forman parte de la ejecución misma. La fecha de Tokio llega con Tyber como un cuerpo de material nuevo, no como una parada de catálogo, y que Japón tenga una sola noche anunciada le da una razón local clara para importar sin convertir artificialmente una fecha de gira mundial en algo irrepetible.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a esta noche si diciembre coincide con Tokio, sobre todo si el viaje trae un hilo de multiinstrumentismo, groove y cruces entre jazz, soul y electrónica. Puede ser una muy buena ancla para una noche en la ciudad, aunque un maestro en un contexto realmente singular o un one-off raro en otro punto de Kanto todavía tendría precedencia.
